title: Context as Architecture, Not a Dump

questions.prompt: A `CLAUDE.md` contains an eight-step release procedure. Where should it live?
options: In `CLAUDE.md`, so it is always loaded and never forgotten
In a skill, so it loads when someone cuts a release and costs nothing otherwise
In a path-scoped rule matching the release script's directory
Nowhere — release procedures cannot be stored as context
questions.explanation: A procedure is a task invoked at a known moment, so a skill is the home: metadata always, body on invoke. Option A makes it a standing charge paid every session for a task you run rarely — the dump pattern. Option C would fire when the release script is edited, not when a release is run, which is the wrong trigger. Option D is false; the question is which layer, not whether.

questions.prompt: A rule says "code under `src/api/` must return this error shape." You start a session to fix a CSS bug in `src/web/`. Which home removes the rule from your window?
questions.explanation: A path-scoped rule loads only when a matching file is read, so a `src/web/` task never pays for it. Option A loads the rule at session start regardless of the task. Option C also loads at startup. Option D would attach the rule to skills you did not invoke, and it would not fire when an API file is edited — the wrong trigger entirely.

questions.prompt: You restart a session. Rank-free: which startup block is NOT re-injected after a `/compact`, even though it was loaded at the start?
questions.explanation: The skill description listing is the block that does not re-inject after compaction; only skills you actually invoked are re-attached. Options A, B, and D are all reloaded — `CLAUDE.md` and memory from disk, the system prompt from the fixed prompt. The trap is assuming every startup block reloads identically; the lifetimes differ, which is the whole point of the architecture.

questions.prompt: Your memory file states "the build command is `pnpm build`", but `package.json` already defines that script. What is the right decision?
options: Keep it — having it in two places is safer
Change it to a path-scoped rule
Delete it — it is derivable from the code, so it is a standing charge with no return
Move it to auto memory so Claude learns it itself
questions.explanation: Content the repo already states is derivable: keeping it in the window costs every session and buys nothing. Option A is the dump instinct — duplication is not safety, it is a second place to go stale. Option B misapplies path scoping to a fact that is not directory-specific. Option D solves the wrong problem; the fact does not need remembering, it needs reading when relevant.
